why:
part of the IMPERATIVE Rust API, which coexists with the declarative component model and is the rclrs-shaped one: `NodeHandle` (exported from `nros` and IN THE PRELUDE, behind `rmw-cffi`) hands back concrete entities you hold and call. rclrs's counterpart exists and correlates by concept but not by name, because ours carries the storage strategy in the type -- `Embedded*` means the entity lives in the executor's static table rather than behind an `Arc`, which is the no-allocator constraint made visible in the name. Which one `nros::` leads with is settled: rclrs's shape, with `nros::Node` as the one node type and the component model as the `nros::Component` / `nros::DeclarativeNode` extension on top (phase-483; issue 0784, resolved).

Issue 2036 (2026-10-25): this verb is the raw, self-deserializing twin of the typed with-info subscription. Its closure takes `(&[u8], Option<&MessageInfo>)`, and it backs the C++ `(msg, const rclcpp::MessageInfo&)` callback through `nros_cpp_subscription_register_message_info`.
